{"body":"FOLR direction discussion: decide whether an explicitly public-lifecycle version of CAMA Traffic Junction warrants one bounded real learned RETAIN-versus-RESET comparison, or preserve the present no-successor boundary.

P77 found a concrete source-interface mismatch: native removal and same-step slot refill can hide a new physical car behind an unchanged mask, while the source controller carries slot memory through inactivity. This issue does not override that finding or treat hidden callbacks as already permitted.

The proposed variant keeps native traffic transitions and reward but openly changes its information protocol. Both arms would receive the same trip-aware state bookkeeping, and both learned actors would receive a global membership-change bit and their own birth bit. New cars start fresh in both; RETAIN keeps true survivors' recurrent history, RESET clears it at actual membership events. A RESET loss would establish only bounded erasure cost, never typed-state novelty or original-task necessity.
